newsitem.title: Jordan: Jordan holds Iraq responsible for driver's death.
newsitem.headline: Jordan holds Iraq responsible for driver's death.

text.p: Jordan said on Tuesday it was holding the Iraqi government responsible for the shooting of one of its embassy drivers on the desert highway to Baghdad.

The Foreign Ministry said in a statement carried by the official Petra news agency it had summoned Iraq's ambassador to Amman to seek information about the attack, which took place on Monday evening about halfway along the 500 km (310 mile) highway between the Jordanian border and Baghdad.
"The ministry contacted the Iraqi ambassador in Amman immediately and asked for details of the incident, holding the Iraqi government completely responsible," said the statement.

The Iraqi embassy in Jordan said it "condemned the criminal attack carried out by an outlaw gang exploiting the exceptional circumstances which Iraq is experiencing because of the sanctions regime imposed upon it."
Ambassador Nouri Ismail el-Weis said in a statement Iraqi authorities were investigating the attack.
He said the driver, Omar Ahmed al-Subh, crossed into Iraq with the the embassy counsellor Fawzi Suleiman. Suleiman, driving his children in a separate car, went on ahead.
Subh's body was found later on Monday night. The killers took the embassy's diplomatic bag which contained 250 Jordanian passports and other documents, he said.
The Jordanian ministry statement said the attack was a violation of international accords guaranteeing the safety of diplomatic couriers.

Jordan, once a close ally of Iraq, stood by its neighbour when a U.S.-led military coalition waged war to expel Baghdad's forces from Kuwait in 1991. But last year King Hussein turned against President Saddam Hussein and called for change in Iraq.
